title: heap overflow in statDecodePage free-chain walk; needs DBSTAT_VTAB
live_proof: fuzz-corpus diff: the image reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as heap-buffer-overflow in statDecodePage at sqlite3.c:177925
arena_bytes_why: 1 MiB on every arm. Five of the eight spatial cases are forced here by reachability -- at 262144 cases 21, 22 and 23 exhaust memsys5 before the defect (pcache1AllocPage dereferences the NULL that 3.22.0 does not check), 29 returns SQLITE_NOMEM, and 00 takes a different path -- so the same value is declared for all eight to keep the arms comparable. Measured 2026-10-17; this is also the value every recorded virtual reading was taken at, while CheriBSD had been running 262144.
object: the page buffer statDecodePage walks while following the free-block chain: iOff = get2byte(&aData[iOff]) inside while( iOff ), with no bound on iOff and no cycle detection. Measured 2026-10-16 by probe site 64: this case takes the free-block chain with iOff=17234 while its cell walk stays within range at 506, the mirror of case 26
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: a corrupt free-block chain sends the walk past the end of the page
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator, with a reconstructed trigger (see case 24, which explains why the SQL for these R2 images had to be re-derived; the old text said case 34, a number from the 38-case corpus that no longer exists). Needs -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DBSTAT_VTAB. Distinct from case 26: the same function, a different walk -- the free-chain traversal rather than the cell-pointer array

spatial.oracle: completes and prints its own marker ('NOTRAP done', rc=0). Recorded as no-marker until 2026-10-05, when the raw log disproved it: the runner had filed it INFRA because the BOOT returned 1 -- the next case in the queue hung -- and charged that to the head of the remaining list. The case's own return code says why nothing was detected: s0_rc=7, SQLITE_NOMEM -- the 256 KB memsys5 arena is exhausted first

sublet.oracle: VM HALTED on a capability fault, cause 24 untagged dereference (temporal: revoked, or never a capability) pc=0x800239e4 -- taken outside the domain, so cooperative recovery has no frame to return through; all 28 halts in this arm are at the same kernel pc 0x800239e4

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes, the mechanism reports nothing. 2026-10-06, CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5, one boot; the run's positive control gate was satisfied before any case ran

status: re-measured on all four readings 2026-10-16 on this platform and every verdict holds. host ASan was re-run on a restored x86 runtime: heap-buffer-overflow in statDecodePage at the free-block chain line, via statNext <- statNext, identical to the 2026-10-11 bundle. virtual-malloc MISSED, RETURNED, both controls as declared. virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=28 pc=0x3fafe1257c in statDecodePage, both controls as declared. cheribsd-revocation MISSED, with the image loaded and the defect reached: probe site 64 reports FREECHAIN iOff=17234, and the run then ends in SQLITE_NOMEM (s1_rc=7) because the 256 KiB arena cannot complete the dbstat scan, which is after the defect site. This arm's 2026-10-06 reading was taken without the image present (see case 21 and the retraction in case 18's PROVENANCE.md), so the MISSED recorded then was a NO-READING; this one is a measured miss. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-17 with one arena on every arm (arena_bytes=1048576) and every arm built from the corpus case.c: virtual-malloc MISSED, virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT cause=28 pc=0x3f94e1257c in statDecodePage, cheribsd-revocation MISSED with RETURNED rc=0 and probe site 64 reporting hits=14 witnesses=13 -- reached and silent, not a no-reading. The earlier spatial readings were taken with the virtual arms at a 1 MiB header default against CheriBSD's 262144, and with this arm compiling its own copy of the case
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16; every verdict holds, and this case is the one that shows what CheriBSD can and cannot see. Probe site 64 hooks all three unchecked reads in statDecodePage. Here the free-block chain runs once with iOff=17234 while the cell walk stays within range at 506 -- the mirror of case 26, which takes the cell walk to 64768 and never enters the chain. Both are over-reads in the same function; the difference is which one the corrupt image steers into. And the consequence for the arms is the distinction the whole spatial group turns on: case 26's walk leaves the WHOLE 256 KiB arena, so CheriBSD's malloc-granularity bounds catch it, while this case's stays inside the arena and that arm is silent. Sublet catches both, because it bounds each sub-allocation. So the two arms are not separated by the defect class here but by the DISTANCE of the over-read, which is a property of the corrupt input. The physical sublet row is one of the 28 halts at kernel pc 0x800239e4 and is marked in results/matrix.tsv; the physical spatial row records a clean completion with the case's own marker, which the virtual-malloc re-run reproduces
fault_sites_why: Host ASan, running the same case source on stock 3.22.0, reports the invalid access in statDecodePage (live_proof); that run is independent of the Capstone arms and predates them.
